# Carlo Alberto Degli Atti (lordkada)

> Innovation, AI & Product Leader based in Milan, Italy, who takes AI and new ideas from prototype to production, including inside large, regulated organisations. Product Lead at PagoPA S.p.A., the state-controlled company behind Italy's public digital payments and services platforms. Serial founder of six companies across Italy and the United States, with two exits, and a computer scientist who still builds hands-on: AI agents, local-first computer vision, and research on artificial valence. Open to Head of Innovation or Chief AI Officer roles, and to product leadership on new products; reachable via LinkedIn.

The site is a single page in two languages. The Italian version is the default; the English one is a translation with the same content.

## Highlights

- PagoPA (2021–now): leads three main initiatives plus early-stage ones, 15–20 people in cross-functional teams (tech, design, legal, account); laid the groundwork for and launched the Developer Portal, the first developer portal of the Italian Public Administration, used by thousands of public bodies and technology partners; released DOS68K, an open-source RAG platform spun off from the portal's AI assistant.
- HELLO Mobility (2020–2021): product manager for the build and production launch of the HELLO app (parking, EV charging, micromobility).
- International STEM Awards (2019–2020): co-founder of a platform for STEM projects by young people aged 7–25; the first edition gathered 118 projects from about 300 participants in 10 countries. Wound down because of the pandemic, still in profit.
- Thingle.me (2015–2019, CEO): customer support software for physical products via QR code or NFC; launched Thingly, a conversational AI assistant for appliances, in 2018. Raised funding, then wound down in a highly competitive market.
- Styloola (2014, CTO): led the development of the Styloola Box, an in-store Wi-Fi analytics device for fashion retail.
- Opinionage (2011–2015, CEO, San Francisco): the social network of opinions, later the HUBNGO community platform for SMEs. Raised funding, then wound down in a highly competitive market.
- Couponline (2004–2009, co-founder and CTO): ScontoQui, personalised coupons delivered at the store entrance. Wound down after much larger competitors crushed it, before its patents could be enforced.
- Concept (2000–2011, CEO, up to 12–15 people): myK, an Enterprise Feedback Management platform listed by Gartner in 2010 among the leading solutions. Exit: sold his shares to his partners.
- Information Delivery Systems (1997–2000, CEO): Business Intelligence consulting boutique founded while at university, grew to 25–30 people. Exit: acquired by a larger company.
